primary: Exploration primary: all externally arrived requests mean completion flow; failures and unfinished cannot be omitted or treated as success. Complete output rate, TTFT, per-request maximum generation gaps, final drain and individual harms are required side effects. Tradeoffs allowed; no post-hoc SLO or significance claim.
slo: No application SLO. Inherited20point frontier is diagnostic only.
hypothesis: At the same native allocation failures, largest immediate physical release may reduce repeated victimization and recovery competition more than preserving shorter declared budgets; conversely sacrificing larger requests may increase their recovery and queue losses. Compare complete service outcomes, not victim count alone.
claim_ceiling: Exploratory direct comparison of two existing simple principles over the complete native legal suffix. Not a novel size/remaining-work method, same-capacity intervention, predicted EOS, full nearest-system reproduction, same-hidden-state replay or independent confirmation.
retention: Keep all cells and failures. At most this one direct endpoint ABBA; no repeated budget-rule test against tail, no tuned size thresholds, no new workload or capacity search.

Prior profile prefix enabled, present original mixed workload prefix disabled; only that engine flag differs intentionally. Not a fresh prefix-off normal profile and not an old-device timing baseline.

Historical max_held_other excludes current and non-pure/private candidates on an older small-KV deployment and does not cover this full-native endpoint.

diagnostic_question: Does more immediate released capacity improve all-arrival mean flow beyond the already-tested simple short-budget protection, once larger victim loss, actual recovery and all other requests are counted?
decision_rule: If max_release consistently improves the frozen primary, accept the ordinary capacity baseline and withdraw investment in budget protection as the preferred principle in this domain. If remaining_budget consistently wins, credit only that known simple principle and report tradeoffs, not novelty. If signs flip or benefit stays unclear within this one group, retain uncertainty and stop adjacent ranking searches in this domain. Zero actual divergence permits only an entry/opportunity diagnosis. No automatic repetitions, threshold rescue, capacity/arrival search or combined predictor; any future investment requires a concrete residual-loss explanation and new discriminating prediction.

budget_mixture.semantics: Assigned maximum output budgets, not future EOS labels. No execution outcomes used. Not a performance-gain comparison with the uniform-budget workload.

runtime_scope: At each allocation-failure decision, both arms observe the same current legal unprocessed suffix and run the same shadows. remaining_budget chooses max(declared max_tokens-output_tokens,index), with phase/protection or any invalid budget falling back to native tail. max_release directly uses the existing max_release_shadow helper: max(immediate_releasable_blocks,index), phase/protection or any unknown physical release falls back to native tail. Physical release counts native non-null unique block references with ref_cnt==1, not held/shared blocks. Current/self, partial-prefill, zero-output, shared and pending-store candidates stay eligible under the existing native lifecycle. Old qualified/fallback_unknown/current_guard do not silently narrow either online rule. Native retry/free/preempt/waiting, Q1, target,1s-trigger,quantum,transfer,admission and inherited observer errors remain fixed.
